concepts.title: Half Right Still Pays the Book
concepts.body: At -110, winning half your spread bets is still short. You need about 52.4% just to break even because the vig is baked into the line.
concepts.takeaway: Check the price before the pick.
concepts.rationale: This turns a familiar confidence trap into one clean number. A player can understand the sportsbook's margin before treating a 50/50 opinion as enough.
concepts.caption: Half right sounds fine until the vig shows up. At standard -110 odds, you need about 52.4% just to break even. Check the price before the pick.
concepts.alt: A Playbook social card for sports betting titled Half Right Still Pays the Book. The body explains that at -110, winning half your spread bets is still short and you need about 52.4% to break even because the vig is baked into the line. The left photo shows adult friends watching sports together. The takeaway says Check the price before the pick.

sources.note: Supports the claim that standard -110 odds require a 52.4% win rate to break even and that the sportsbook's line accounts for available information.
Explains vig as the sportsbook's built-in commission and states that -110 means betting $110 to win $100.
Lists -110 at a 52.4% break-even rate. Arithmetic: 110 / (110 + 100) = 52.38%, rounded to 52.4%.

concepts.title: Almost Is Just Theater
concepts.body: A slot near miss feels close, but the RNG already chose the result before the reels moved. The next spin starts fresh; the last display has no vote.
concepts.takeaway: Near misses do not warm up the next spin.
concepts.rationale: The hook respects the feeling of a near miss while naming what actually happened. It gives the player a useful rule without mocking the ritual or the reaction.
concepts.caption: Two symbols and a blank can feel like the game winked at you. It did not. The RNG already picked the result, and the next spin starts fresh.
concepts.alt: A Playbook myth-check card titled Almost Is Just Theater. The body explains that a slot near miss feels close, but the RNG already chose the result before the reels moved, and the next spin starts fresh. The left photo shows adult friends in a warm casino lounge with blurred slot lights behind them. The takeaway says Near misses do not warm up the next spin.

sources.section: Myth 4: Near Misses Mean You're Close
sources.note: Supports the claim that a near miss is not almost winning and that the result was decided when the player pressed spin.
Explains that the RNG generates the result, maps it to symbols, and the reels display an outcome already decided before animation.
Supports the takeaway that every spin is independent and past spins have zero effect on the next one.

concepts.title: Price the Night First
concepts.body: Your entertainment budget is the cost of the session, decided before the action starts. Once play gets loud, the best number is the one you already picked.
concepts.takeaway: Pick the number while the room is quiet.
concepts.rationale: This keeps the tools message in Tier 1: practical, self-directed, and tied to entertainment value. It focuses on a decision made before the energy of play changes the mood.
concepts.caption: The cleanest budget decision happens before the room gets loud. Pick the cost of the session first, then let the night be entertainment.
concepts.alt: A Playbook your-play card titled Price the Night First. The body explains that an entertainment budget is the cost of the session, decided before action starts, and that the best number is the one already picked.
